text: SCHOOL-BASED PROGRAMS. The Department of Education (DepEd), through its Division Office and in coordination with the Child Protection Committee (CPC) created within the school, shall aid in strengthening children protection against sexual abuse through the following measures and strategies: 1. Conduct various advocacies, campaigns and other forms of information dissemination activities for purposes of raising awareness on children protection against sexual abuse in a school-setting. The Division Office may coordinate with the City Information Office for purposes of implementing this provision. 2. Formulate and implement child protection policies, guidelines and procedures for quick response and appropriate referral system for purposes of enhancing and strengthening child protection and safety against sexual abuse in a school-setting. 3. In coordination with CSWDO and SOCC, conduct training for teachers and other school personnel relating to protection of children against sexual abuse in a school-setting such as: a. Equipping them with the ability to recognize potential indicators of sexual abuse incidents among the students; b. Equipping them with the ability to influence children in mentally conditioning them on how to protect themselves from the vices of sexual abuse and their vulnerability to it. They shall aid in building resiliency, self-esteem and psychological competence of students against sexual abuse through providing them appropriate information knowledge and skills; c. Conduct training in handling incidents of sexual abuse committed to students specifically on repofting to appropriate agencies including referral to rehabilitation centers, providing comfort to victims and maintaining the confidentiality thereof; d. Ensure that they are well-oriented with laws relating to sexual abuse, including this Ordinance, and determine their duties and the rights of the students embodied therein; e. Members of the Committee on Decorum and Investigation (CODI) and other officers created pursuant to Safe Spaces City Ordinance of Davao City shall participate in the training and be equipped with competence to handle cases of sexual abuse involving children; PageT of 15 Ord. No. 0854-22 4. Develop and incorporate in the curriculum of the children in public or private schools with information that will enable them to understand the vices of sexual abuse and their vulnerability to it and mentally condition in them the necessity to protect themselves from it. Also, develop age-appropriate, gender-sensitive and cultural-appropriate information materials relating to protection of children against sexual abuse. The DepEd, in coordination with IGDD and CSWDO, shall provide Child Protection Policy Modules to fufther strengthen the city's child protection program and empower children to seek protection against abusers. Encourage the students to provide anti-sexual abuse activities to be included in the plans of the student government/councils, clubs or organizations, cocurricular activities and other school-based programs; 5. Establish a Master list and Database on Students where records pertaining to the information of students shall be kept confldentially; 6. Provide a Situation Assessment and Analysis to determine who are those students that are considered at high-risk of being sexually abused. The Situation Analysis can be used to determine the school-based risk factors and conditions that contribute to incidents of sexual abuse on children. It shall also give recommendations to the Committee necessary to enhance and strengthen the protection of children against sexual abuse. 7. Ensure that hotlines and other venues for repofting incidents of sexual abuse are posted in the conspicuous premises of the school. B. It shall serue as repository of information related to sexual abuse in schoolsetting and shall maintain reports of incidents and cases of all schools. The records shall be confidential and only upon the request of proper agencies such as the Committee, coufts, police and others that the same shall be disclosed. 9. Provide for other mechanisms that will further enhance and strengthen protection of children against sexual abuse and develop a safe and protective environment. The provisions laid down in DepEd Order No. 40, SERIES of 2012, shall apply herein suppletorily. ROLE OF CITY SOCIAL WELFARE AND DEVELOPMENT OFFICE (CSWDO)

The CSWDO shall also conduct life-skill trainings to the members of the family. a) Children should be able to learn life-skills against all forms of sexual abuse such as, but not limited to, the following: Recognition skills - A child should be able to determine sexual invitations and innuendos of the perpetrator. He or she should also be able to identify risk indicators such as when he or she is isolated with a stranger. Fufther, he or she should become more cautious and vigilant in the place and people around him or her. Communication skills - Knowing how to refuse sexual invitations and innuendos of the perpetrator. Practical and feasible self-defense skills - it may tap the DCPO or other agencies with competency to provide such skills. Repofting skills - A child should be guided where to report incidents and seek aid. These may include parents, relatives, teachers, barangay officials, police officers, and hotlines. That if he or she is threatened, the child should be able to know how he/she can seek assistance and whom he or she can approach. b) Parents and other persons with parental authority shall be equipped with skills appropriate for protecting the child from any forms of sexual abuse such as, but not limited to, the following: iv t ii. iii i. text: VISITATION POWERS (a) As an incident to its mandated duty under SECTION 9 of this Ordinance, the City Government of Davao, through the IACAT-DC, in coordination with the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) and the Davao City Police Office Ord. No. 0532-18 (DCPO) shall conduct inspection, in coordination with proper authorities, of rooms, houses, buildings or establishments repofted as being used for trafficking activities, or in the course of regular and/or routinary inspection. The authorities shall have access to the employer's records and premises and the right to copy therefrom, to question any employee and investigate any fact or matter which may be necessary to determine if there are trafficking activities. (b) The unjustifiable refusal of the owner or person in charge of any room, house, building or establishment to submit the same for inspection by the city officials and authorities shall give rise to the prima facie presumption of willfully impeding and/or obstructing the mandated duty of the City Government to monitor and document trafficking cases, and may expose said owner or person in charge to possible prosecution for violation of this Ordinance; (c) The Local Government shall formulate the proper guidelines and protocols that will be obserued in the exercise of this power, in order to ensure compliance SECTION L2. CANCELLATION OF LICENSES OF ESTABLISHMENTS WHICH VIOLATE THE PROVISIONS OF R.A. NO. 9208 AS AMENDED AND EXPANDED BY R.A. 10364 (a) The Office of the City Mayor shall effect the cancellation or revocation of the business permits and/or licenses of any individual or establishment found to have violated the provisions of R.A. No. 9208 as amended and expanded by R.A. 10364. (b) All managers or owners of establishments applying for new business permits and/or licenses or applying for renewal thereof shall undergo an anti-trafficking seminar conducted by the IACAT-DC and sign a written undeftaking that they shall not employ minors who are victims of trafflcking. Bars, nightclubs, videoke/KTV Bars, and other similar establishments providing adult amusement or entertainment, as well as factories/plants, poultry, piggery and other agricultural structures, or other labor-intensive establishments, shall be required to keep copies of Philippine Statistics Authority (pSA) authenticated birth ceftificates of all employees as proof of age, and provide other prooi of identification with recent photo of the employee duly issued by the government such as NBI, Police, Postal or Barangay Clearance/ID. The managers and owners as mentioned shall be required to conduct or attend anti-trafficking in persons seminar prior to the issuance or renewal of their license or business permit. (c) All boarding houses, pension houses, dormitories and similar establishments that provide temporary or permanent lodging facilities for the purpose of generating any rental/lease income, shall be required to apply for business permits and/or licenses. The owner, proprietor or manager of any such establishment applying for new business permits and/or licenses or applying for renewal thereof, shall sign a notarized written undeftaking that they shall not engage in any acts, which promote trafficking such as, but not limited to, allowing the use of their premises to such acts. Further, the said establishment shall have the mandatory duty to report suspected cases of trafficking to the IACAT-DC. (d) The refusal and/or failure to sign the above-mentioned undertaking or the subsequent violation of the same, or the failure to keep employees' birth certificates as required under paragraph (b), or the possession of falsified bifth certificates in the records of employment, or the failure to report suspected cases of trafficking to the IACAT-DC or the POEA or other local authorities, shall constitute a ground for immediate denial or cancellation of the business permit and/or licenses of the individual or the establ ishment concerned, Ord. Davao was the last unoccupied territory in the Philippines and Datu Bago heroically defended it against the Spaniards.

text: ADDRESSING BULLYING IN EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIOilS -All educationa! institutions are hereby directed to adopt policies to address the existence of bullying. Such policies shall be regularly updated and, at a minimum, shall include provisions which: A.Identify the range of disciplinary administrative actions that may be taken against a respondent for bullying or retaliation which shall be commensurate with the nature and gravity of the offense: Provided, that, in addition to the disciplinary sanctions imposed upon a respondent of bullying or retaliation, he/she shall also be required to undergo a rehabilitation program which shall be administered by the institution concerned. The parents of the said respondent shall be encouraged by the said institution to join the rehabilitation program. 'i Page 5 of 10. O'rd. No. 0L92-23. B. Establish clear procedures and strategies for: 1. Reporting acts of bullying or retaliation; 2. Responding promptly to and investigating reports of bullying or retaliation; 3. Restoring a sense of safety for a victim and assessing the student's need for protection; 4. Protecting from bullying or retaliation of a person who reports acts of bullying, provides information during an investigation of bullying, or is witness to or has reliable information about an act of bullying; and 5. Providing counseling or referral to appropriate services for respondents, complainants, and appropriate family members of said students. C.Enable students to anonymously report bullying or retaliation: Provided, however, that no disciplinary administrative action shall be taken against a respondent solely on the basis of an anonymous report; D.Subject a student who knowingly makes a false accusation of bullying to disciplinary administrative action; E. Educate students on the dynamics of bullying, the anti-bullying policies of the school as well as the mechanisms of such school for the anonymous reporting of acts of bullying or retaliation; F. Educate parents and guardians about the dynamics of bullying, the anti-bullying policies of the school and how parents and guardians can provide support and reinforce such policies at home; and G.Maintain a public record of relevant information and statistics on acts of bullying or retaliation in school: Provided, that the names of students who committed acts of bullying or retaliation shall be strictly confidential and only made available to the school administration, teachers directly responsible for the said students and parents or guardians of students who are or have been victims of acts of bullying or retaliation. All educational institutions shall provide students and their parents or guardians a copy of the anti-bullying policies being adopted by the school. Such policies shall likewise be included in the school's student and/or employee handbook and shall be conspicuously posted on the school walls and website, if there is any. Training programs, courses, or activities which shall provide opportunities for school administrators, teachers, and other employees to develop their knowledge and skills in preventing or responding to acts of bullying shall also be performed in these educational institutions.

text: ACTS OF BULLYING -"Bullying" as adopted from Republic Act No. 10627, shall refer to any severe or repeated act by one or more persons through a written, verbal or electronic expression, or a physical act or gesture, or any combination thereof, directed at another individual that has the effect of actually causing or placing the latter in reasonable fear of physical or emotional harm to himself or damage to his propefi; creating a hostile environment at the schoo!, workplace, or any other situation for the individual; infringing on the rights of the individual; or materially and substantially disrupting the education process or the orderly operation of a school, workplace, or any other area, venue, or situation; such as, but not limited to, the following: a) Any unwanted physical contact between the bully and the complainant, such as punching, pushing, shoving, kicking, slapping, tickling, headlocks, inflicting pranks, teasing, fighting and the use of available objects as weapons; b) Any act that causes damage to an individual's psyche and/or emotional well-being; c) Any slanderous statement or accusation that causes an individual undue emotional distress, such as directing foul language or profanity at the target, name-calling, tormenting and commenting negatively on an individual's looks, clothes and body; d) Cyberbullying or any bullying done through the use of technology or any electronic means. Bullying shall be further classified into four (4) aspects, namely: a. Bullying in educational institutions b. Bullying in the workplace c. Cyberbullying d. Bullying in other public places Any person who commits the acts described above is considered a bully. Persons who, through the acts described above, retaliate against another person who repofts acts of bullying or who provides information during an investigation or is a witness under such investigation, shall also be considered to have committed bullying. Any unwanted physical contact between the bully and the victim like punching, pushing, shoving, kicking, slapping, tickling, headlocks, inflicting school pranks, teasing, fighting and the use of available objects as weapons; 2. Any act that causes damage to a victim's psyche and/or emotional well-being; 3. Any slanderous statement or accusation that causes the victim undue emotional distress like directing foul language or profanity at the target, name-calling, tormenting and commenting negatively on victim's looks, clothes and body. Educational institutions covered under this Ordinance include public or private schools, regardless of educational level, such as: a) Preparatory schools; b) Primary schools; c) Secondary schools; d) Colleges and universities, including post-graduate; e) Vocational schools; 0 Review centers, tutorial centers, and other similar establishments; g) Training institutions by virtue of education such as On-the-Job training as well as other activities performed off-school, but for educational purpose/s. Persons liable for bullying under this SECTION include, but are not limited to, the following: i. Students; ii. Trainees, interns, exchange students, and volunteers; iii. Teachers, student-teachers and non-teaching staff; iv. School Administrators; v. Parents and guardians of students; vi. Other authorized persons within the school campus; vii. Visitors. All acts and repofts of bullying in the aforementioned institutions, and al! acts of bullying by, among, and between the aforementioned persons shall be under the primary jurisdiction of the educational institution concerned.

text: DECLARATION OF PRINCIPLES AND POLICIES A. The City Government of Davao is committed to the maintenance of peace and security within its jurisdiction, as a safe and peaceful environment is vital to the progress of a city when there are no risks and threats to its development. B. Implementing and policymaking bodies are created for the purpose of peacebuilding. C. Therc are eight (8) broad categories that create and sustain peaceful societies. The Institute for Economics and Peace has identified the following eight (8) Pillars of PosiUve Peace as the most common characteristics of most peaceful societies. These pillars are: . Well-functioning government; o Low levels of corruption; . Acceptance of the rights of others; . Good relations with neighbors; . Sound business environment; o High level of human capital; . Equitable distribution of resources; and o Free flow of information. The concept of Positive Peace acknowledges that ending direct violence alone does not guarantee durable peace. Ending direct violence is Negative Peace. For peace to endure, a society must build longer-term conditions that enable society to unify and flourish. This is called Positive Peace. Investing in Positive Peace improves resilience, mitigates risks of violence, and reduces the economic toll from conflict. The Eight-Pillars of Positive Peace are highly interconnected and interact together to build a system. It therefore requires building capacities for peace, not only of the government, but also of local communities and other structures and institutions of the city. The establishment of Peace 911- The Center For Peacebuilding will contribute to the achievement of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals of the United Nations, in particular, Goal 16 on building peace, justice and strong institutions, strengthening human rights, reducing discrimination and inequality, promoting gender equality, preseruing natural resources and protecting the climate. D. Republic Act TLGI SECTION 3(b) states that there shall be established in every local government unit an accountable, efficient, and dynamic organizational structure and operating mechanism that will meet the priority needs and seruice requirements of its communities; and 3 (h) there shall be a continuing mechanism to enhance local autonomy not only by legislative enabling acts but also by administrative and organizational reforms. Ord. No. 0891-22 E. Republic Act 7160, SECTION 76 states that every local government unit shall design and implement its own organizational structure and staffing pattern taking into consideration its service requirements and financial capacity, subject to the minimum standards and guidelines prescribed by the Civil Service Commission. text: GENERAL PROVISTONS. a. Appraisal by Stripping Method shall be adopted where 100o/o base value per square meter on residential and commercial lands shall be applied within the first strip fronting roads or streets. Land beyond the standard depth, that is, 20m for residential, 30m for commercial and 50m for industrial shall be valued at 80o/o for the 2nd strip, 600/o for the 3d strip, 40o/o for the 4h strip, 20o/o for the 5h strip of the base value fixed for the road or street thereof for the remaining area, provided that, the value per square meter of the last strip shall not be lower than the value per square meter of lots in the other street or of the interior lots as reflected in the Schedule of Market Value. Stripping Method shall not apply to corner lots if the sides are less than the standard depth. b, Subdivision lots are not subject to stripping. c. For abnormally low lands, a reduction from the base unit value may be allowed in the amount to the cost of fllling-up of such land, provided that, such deduction shall not exceed 30o/o of the value of the lot subject to appraisal if it were normally filled or leveled. d. Corner influence of 100/o of the base unit value shall be added to residential and commercial lots situated at the corner of the streets or roads. Provided that, if the streets or roads have different base unlt value, the higher value shall be used in the computation. An alley or callejon shall not be considered for the adjustment thereof. e. Roads or streets in urban subdivisions, unless already donated or turned over to the barangay or city, shall be listed in the name of the subdivision owner and shall be valued on the basis of the actual condition and cost of cementing, asphalting or paving them with gravel and sand per square meter. f. Vacant lands shall be classified, valued and assessed like similar lands in the area. g. Urban land fully occupied by squatters who prevented the owner from using or making developments of the subject lot, park and open spaces shall be valued at 50o/o of the base value. Ord. No. 0257-17 h. Interior lots shall be valued at 50% of the base value of the lots fronting primary road or street, however stripping method shall not be applied. i. Triangular lot with its base on the street shall be computed as a regular lot with 70olo base value. j. Triangular lot with its apex on the street shall be computed as a regular lot with 30% base value. k. Trapezoid Lots shall be computed based on the values of the rectangular and triangular portions separately and to take the sum of the computed values for the total value. m. Lots along concrete roads shall have a 100o/o base value,95% base value for dirt road and 80% base value for alley and proposed road. 2. Appraisal of Agricultural Lands (a)The unit base value per hectare prescribed in the SMV is multiplied by the area of the agricultural land to arrive at the market value for the different kinds and sub-classes of agricultural lands. Apparently, the kind of plants and trees determine the classification and value of the agricultural land. The aggregate value arrived at is subject to applicable adjustments expressed in percentage, to wit: (1) Type of Road % Adjustment (a) Provincial or national road (b) For all-weather roads No deduction 3% deduction c Alo dirt roads 6% deduction d For no road outlet 9% deduction (2) Location Distance in Km to: (a) All weather roads (b) Local Trading Center (Poblacion) 0to 1 +SYo Over 1 to 3 -2% 0% Over 3 to 6 -2Yo -6% -4Yo Over 9 -8% -6% l. Irregular Lot shall be computed by reducing the irregular lot to the nearest equivalent rectangular, triangular and trapezoidal sections and apply the foregoing rules in computing lot values, -4% Over 6 to 9 Ord. No. 0257-17 The distance of a property from all-weather roads, landing places along sea coasts and from a trading center or poblacion shall be measured from the corner of the lot or parcel nearest to such road or center. All weather roads include national, provincial, municipal and all other public roads traversable by trucks, cars and other forms of vehicles under any kind of weather. (b)The computation of values begins with the determination of the area, productivity and sub-class or sub-classes of an agricultural land. In the case of a parcel of land utilized or planted to various agricultural crops, such as, rice, corn, coconut, etc. (if practicable, the boundaries between each sub-class shall be plotted or sketched on the map) and the corresponding area thereof be determined. Each area so determined shall be multiplied by the applicable unit base value. The resulting values for each sub-class so computed are summed up to obtain the total base market value of the parcel. To arrive at a final value, the total base market value is multiplied by the adjustment percentage, as stated above. (c) Values of improvement such as plants and trees shall be considered in the preparation of the Schedule of Values for agricultural lands. Although these crops are deemed improvemenG to the land, they shall not be appraised apart from the land as they are an integral part thereof and their value is inherent or forms part of the land. However, if it shall be proven that the ownership of the land is different from that of the improvement, a separate valuation and assessment shall be made in the names of the respective owners. (d)Agricultural land convertible into residential subdivisions, commercial or industrial land shall be classified and valued as agricultural until such time that they shall have been actually converted and developed into such. This rule shall also apply to lands already approved by proper authorities as subdivisions but have not yet been actually developed for the purpose. As soon as a portion of the subdivision is finally divided, converted and developed into residential lots, the same shall be valued like similar lots in the locality. Portions of the subdivisions not yet developed and converted into residential, commercial or industrial lot shall remain to be classified and valued as agricultural. Portions of agricultural land not yet developed, converted and actually used as residential, commercial or industrial shall remain to be classified and valued as agricultural. 3. Appraisal of Timber and Forest Lands llmber and forest lands belonging to the Republic of the Philippines or any of its political subdivisions, the beneficial use of which have been granted to a taxable person, shall be subject to the real property tax. For this purpose, said lands shall be appraised and assessed yearly against the beneficial useratthe market value ofthe marketable timber on the Ord. No. 0257-77 basis of the annual volume of timber "actually cut" from the operational area, during the preceding year, regardless of the annual total .'allowable cut" indicated in the lease agreement. 4. Appraisal of Mineral Lands (a) Mineral lands are those lands in which minerals exist in sufficient quantity or grade to justify the necessary expenditures to be incurred in extracting and utilizing such minerals. (b) Mineral lands are further classified as follows: 2. Non-Metallic Mineral Lands These are lands which contain all other deposits not covered by the above-deflned metallic elements or minerals. (c) Mineral Lands shall be appraised yearly against the beneficial user or concessionaire on the basis of the value of extracted minerals. 5. Appraisal of Buildings (a) For the appraisal of buildings and other structures, the schedule of Base Unit construction cost (SBUCC) shall be used. The sBUCC refers to the base unit construction cost of buildings per square meter including the additional/deduction items as may be determined by the assessor. However, buildings and other structures not included in the sBucc shall be appraised based on the actual cost (b) In case of a multi-storey building used both for residential and commercial or industrial purposes, the same shall be classified and valued in accordance with the type of building provided in the schedule of Base unit construction Cost and shall be assessed on the basis of the actual use of such building. (c) Bowling alleys shall be initially valued separately from the principal building but its appraisal/assessment shall finally form part of the whole building, except the machinery, which shall be covered by a separate appraisal and assessment. (d) In case of buildings and structures already covered by existing assessment, the Reproduction/Replacement Cost New Less Depreciation (RCNLD) approach shall be applied. (e) Inspection Levels - The level of property inspection depends on the quality of the Field Appraisal Assessment Sheet (FAAS's) and various other factors such as: 1. Metallic Mineral Lands These are lands which contain any of the metallic elements or minerals, or their combinations such as gold, silver, platinum, tin, chromium, iron, manganese, copper, nickel, lead, zinc, tungsten, and the like. Ord. No. 0257-t7 1, Years of last re-appraisal/revision of assessment; 2. Level of new construction; 3. Local changes; 4. Higher than normal appeal activity; 5. Inconsistent or incorrect classification of buildings or land; 6. Changes in the market area such as area redevelopment, increased density, use or zoning; 7. The need to redefine market area boundaries and establish new benchmarks; 8. Change in market preferences for factors such as house style/age, lot size, market area characteristics, traffic patterns, etc; 9. Changes in building costs because of changes in code requirements, new materials/designs, etc; and 10, Changes in market perception from positive or negative factors; Correcting appraisal deficiencies generally require some level of physical inspection of the property. Different levels of inspection will be required depending upon the reason(s) found for the deficiency. The following are generally accepted definitions for the various levels of inspections: Level 1. A full inspection is made with a full interior inspection. Level 2. An exterior inspection is made. No attempt at an interior inspection is made unless a major change to the property is detected. Level 3. A street inspection is conducted. (Drive-by inspection only, unless a major change to the property is detected.) 6. Appraisal of Machinery and Equipment (a) The appraisal of machinery for tax purposes shall be based on its actual cost to the owner. To support the actual cost, the declared value or sworn statement from the owner or responsible officer, in case of a corporation, shall be secured to form as an integral part of the appraisal report. (b) For imported brand new machinery, the market value shall be based on its acquisition cost, which is the actual cost to the owner when the same is not yet depreciated or appraised within the year of its purchase, plus the costs of freigh,t, insurance, bank and other charges, brokerage, arrastre and handling, duties and taxes, plus the costs of inland transpoftation, handling and installation charges at the present site. The cost in foreign currency shall be converted to peso cost on the basis of the foreign currency exchange rates when such machinery was actually purchased as fixed by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP). Level 4. No on-site inspection is made. Ord. No. 0257-17 (c) By the expressed provision of the Local Government Code, the acquisition cost of the machinery shall be based on the actual cost to the owner when it was acquired. The cost in foreign currency shall be converted to peso cost based on the foreign exchange rate then prevailing when the same was acquired. (d) In all other cases, the cost in foreign currency of imported machinery shall be converted to peso equivalent based on exchange rates flxed by the BSp at the time of acquisition and apply a depreciation allowance of not exceeding five percent (5%) per year. (g) Transmission Lines, Transmission Towers, Cell Sites and the like shall be assessed like all other machineries and taxes thereon shall be paid to the local government unit where they are constructed. Transmission lines including the posts shall be appraised on the basis of its total value using the cost or income approach and the total market value shall also be apportioned or pro-rated between the local government units where these lines traverse. (h) Submerged pipe lines for natural gas, water, etc., shall be appraised on the basis of the cost or income approach, the total market value thereof shall be apportioned or pro-rated between the local government units they traverse. Ord. No. 0257-17 (i) Reservoirs, dams, tailing ponds, piers and wharyes shall be appraised on the basis of the cost approach, Provided, however, that the cost of pilings on ports must be given additional consideration. 7. Appraisal of Special Purpose Properties (1) Special purpose properties such as golf course, memorial park, cemeteries, hospitals, schools, malls, shopping centers, gasoline stations and condominiums, are properties which are designed, constructed and developed for a specific use or purpose. By its very nature the type of property is rarely offered for sale in the open market as part of a going concern. Due to its special design and function, conversion of special purpose properties to other types of development or application is generally not economically feasible. (2) In valuing special purpose properties, the appraiser shall be guided with the provisions in SECTION 8, Chapter IV of the Local Assessment Regulation (LAR) 1-04 issued by the Bureau of Local Government Finance - Department of Finance (BLGF-DOF). C. Rules in the Assessment of Real Property All real propertles, whether taxable or exempt, shall be appraised based on the applicable Schedule of Market Values for Lands (SMV) and Base Unit Construction Cost (BUCC) prepared by the City Assessor. Real property declared for the first time shall be assessed for the period during which it would have been liable but in no case for more than ten (10) years prior to the date of initial assessment: Provided, however, that such taxes shall be computed on the basis of the applicable schedule of values in force during the corresponding period. Provided further, that the total tax liability shall include the current year in addition to the ten (10) years back taxes. If such taxes are paid on or before the end of the quarter following the date the notice of assessment was received by the owner or his representative, no interest for delinquency shall be imposed thereon; otheruvise, such taxes shall be subject to an interest at the rate of two percent (2o/o) per month or a fraction thereof until such taxes are fully paid. 1. Assessment of Lands (a) Lands actually and principally used for residential, agricultural, commercial, industrial or mineral purposes, shall be classified and valued according to the schedule of unit base market values and assessed at their corresponding levels of assessment. (b) Lands located in areas of mixed land uses such as residential with commercial or industrial, the predominant use of the lands in that area shall govern the classification and valuation thereof. If the predominant use is residential, all lands in that area shall be classified as residential; if the predominant use is commercial or industrial, all lands in that area shall be classified as such. Ord. No. 0257-77 (c) A lot or parcel of land classified and appraised as commercial or industrial occupied by a building used both for residential and commercial or industrial purposes shall be assessed on the basis of the predominant use of the building or buildings. If the predominant use of the building is residential, the assessment level fixed thereon for residential land shall be applied on the market value of the lot or parcel determined on the basis ofthe schedule of base market values; if industrial or commercial, the assessment level for industrial or commercial shall be applied on the basis of the schedule of base market values. (d) Vacant lands shall be assessed like similar lands in the locality. (e) Lands owned by local water districts and government-owned or controlled corporations rendering essential public services in the supply and distribution of water and/or generation and transmission of electric power, located in residential, commercial or industrial area shall be assessed as special property at ten percent (100/o) assessment level applied to the market value. If those special classes of lands are, however, located in areas of mixed land uses, such as residential with commercial or industrial, the predominant use of the lands in that area of those special classes of land shall be assessed at the corresponding levels of assessment. (f) Lands actually, directly and exclusively used for religious, charitable or educational purposes located in residential, commercial or industrial areas shall be assessed as residential, commercial or industrial, as the case may be. If those lands actually, directly and exclusively used for religious, charitable or educational purposes are, however, located in an area of mixed land uses, such as residential with commercial or industrial, the predominant use of the lands in that area shall govern the classification of those lands used for religious, charitable or educational purposes. However, if those lands are occupied by a building used both for educational, residential, commercial or Industrial, the area of land occupied by the building and its premises shall be assessed as residential, commercial or industrial as the case may be. (g) Reclassification of Lands to Other Uses 1. Land converted into other uses, e,g. agricultural to residential, residential to commercial, made known to the assessor in writing by the owner shall be inspected for confirmation of the actual condition/use of the property; Ord. No. 0257-t7 2. A report of the actual condition of the property and the recommendation thereof shall be rendered by the responsible personnel. Such report shall be submitted within ten (10) working days after inspection in accordance with the policy as may be prescribed by the City Assessor; 3. Among others, the report may contain information regarding tangible land improvement, e.g. land leveling and compaction, construction of road networks, drainage and other relevant land amenities; 4. In all other cases, Local Finance Circular No. 3-92 dated September LL, 1992 shall be controlling in reclassifying agricultural lands to non-agricultural uses; and 5. A duly approved Zoning Ordinance also serves as basis in the reclassifi cation of lands. 6. Sworn statement declaring the true value and classiflcation by the owner. 2. Assessment of Buildings and Other tmprovements (a) Buildings used exclusively for residential purposes shall be classified and valued in accordance with the schedule of base unit construction cost, and shall be assessed by applying the corresponding assessment levels fixed by ordinances of the SANGGUNIANG panlungsod. (b)A one-storey building used both for residential and commercial or industrial purposes shall be classified and valued in accordance with the schedule of base unit construction cost and shall be assessed on the basis of the predominant use of the building. (c) A multi-storey building used both for residential and commercial or industrial and any other purposes shall be classified and valued in accordance with the type of building provided in the SBUCC and shall be assessed on the basis of its actual use. (d) Buildings and other improvements actually, directly and exclusively used for hospitals, cultural or scientific purposes shall be classified and valued according to the schedule of base unit construction cost, and shall be assessed at 15olo of their depreciated market values. (e) Buildings owned by local water districts and Government-Owned or Controlled Corporations rendering essential public services in the supply and distribution of water and/or generation and transmission of electric power shall, likewise be classified and valued in accordance with the schedule of base unit construction cost, and shall be assessed at 10o/o of their depreciated value. Ord. No. 0257-17 (f,) Churches, parsonages, convents, mosques and buildings and other improvements used actually, directly and exclusively for religious, charitable or educational purposes shall be classified and valued in accordance with the schedule of base unit construction cost, if applicable, othenrrise on the basis of their replacement cost as of the year of appraisal, and shall be assessed as residential on the basis of their depreciated values. (g) Buildings and other improvements owned by the Republic of the Philippines or any of its political subdivisions shall be classified, valued and assessed like similar buildings and improvements in the locality. If the buildings and improvements are of a kind not covered by the schedule of base unit construction cost, they shall be valued at their fair market value at the time of appraisal and shall be assessed like similar buildings and improvements in the locality. D. Notice of New or Revised Assessments (1) When real propefi is assessed for the first time or when an existing assessment is increased or decreased, the City Assessor shall within thirty (30) days give written notice of such new or revised assessment to the person in whose name the property is declared. (2)Although the real property tax is levied against real property, it is the owner who pays the tax. Before the tax liability is fixed, the property owner is entitled to a hearing on the assessment of the property; notice and hearing constitute part of the due process (not strictly judicial) in taxation. If the owner is not satisfied with the action of the assessor in the assessment of the property, the said owner can resoft to the appeals process provided in Chapter VII of Local Assessment Regulation (LAR) 1-04. If he does not appeal within the said period, he will be deprived of his right to be heard by the Board of Assessment Appeals (LBAA). However, in cases where a request is made by the person in whose name the propefty is declared to correct erroneous or illegal assessments, the Assessor, after re-inspection and report of actual condition and recommendation by responsible personnel, may correct and adjust the assessment previously made without necessarily referring to LBAA. But, once the Notice of Re-Assessment has been sent to the propefty owner, assessment/re-assessment is beyond the authority of the assessor and is already under the jurisdiction of the Local Board of Assessment Appeals (LBAA). a. The written notice together with the owner's copy of the tax declaration shall be addressed to the person in whose name the propefty is declared. It may be delivered personally or to the occupant in possession of the property, or by mail to the last known address of the owner or thru the assistance of the punong barangay. Ord. No. 0257-17 b. If personally delivered to the owner or person in possession of the property, the person serving the notice shall secure the signature of the owner or occupant on the duplicate copy of the notice, with a notation of the date when the notice was served and whether recipient is the owner or occupant of the property. If assistance of the punong barangay is secured, the signature should appear on the duplicate copy of the notice. The duplicate copies of the notice of assessments signed by the owners or occupants of the property and the registry return cards shall be flled in the office of the city assessor and annotated on the Field Appraisal Assessment Sheet (FAAS) that such Notice of Assessment (NOA) has been issued indicating the name of the person who received the Notice of Assessment (NOA), date and time received, These are important in asceftaining whether appeals filed by owners of real property are filed within the reglamentary period of sixty days from the date of receipt of such notices.

text: BUILDING PERMIT PROCESSING TIME _ The different offices involved in the OSSCP, functioning as one unit, shall evaluate simple Building Permit applications with complete documentary requirements, within a maximum period of five (5) working days. The Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) shall process the Fire Safety Evaluation Clearance (FSEC) within a maximum period of three (3) working days and shall abide by the manual operations that will be developed in relation to Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2018-01 dated January 4,20L8 issued by the Depaftment of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICD and the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) and other supplemental manuals that shall be separately prepared by individual OSSCP. For easy compliance by the applicant, applications with deficiencies shall be issued a Comprehensive Correction Sheet and/or a Notice of Disapproval by the Zoning Officer, City Building Official (OBO), and the local Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) stating all deflciencies. For applications that satisfy the requirements of the Zoning Ordinance, the OSSCP shall release the Building Permit, together with the locational clearance, other ancillary permits and the Fire Safety Evaluation Clearance (FSEC,) after payment of appropriate fees and charges. The Office of the City Building Official (OBO) shall provide the local BFP and the City Assessor's Office with the list of the issued Building Permits on a monthly basis (every 5th day of the month) for their reference, in anticipation of the applicant's future application for a Ceftiflcate of Occupancy.

USES OF THE PREMISES - The LESSEE shall not use the leased premises for dwelling or sleeping purposes. The premises hereby leased shall be used exclusively by the LESSEE for office, stockroom and related purposes and the latter shall not divert the prernises to any other uses without the prior consent of the LESSOR, it being expressly agreed that if, at any time during the existence of this Iease and without the previous consent of the LESSOR the said prernises is used for any other purposes, the LESSOR reserves the right or choice to, (a) rescind this contract in accordance with Paragraph 17, (b) increase the rental, or (c) compel the LESSEE to stop its new activities. 4. The LESSOR reserves the right to refuse any alteration, installation, addition or improvement requested by the LESSEE if in the LESSOR'S opinion, there is just cause to warrant such refusal. 5.
